messages.subject: Range Selection DT Shiny
parts:
Hi everyone, 

I am trying to expand my application for my company a bit and I cannot seem to find any articles online that would assist me in this. I am attempting to use the DT library range selector but I want to use it in a non-conventional sense. 

I am currently using the DT library for its row selection features. The user will essentially choose a column(s) and, from that, the DT is auto generated with only unique values from the column(s) selected. When someone wants to choose a unique value to plot on the graph they simply click the value and the plot is generated the N values that are currently under the rows_selected category. 

My question is this, is there a way, if the user utilizes the range selection in association with DT filtering, that I can retrieve the selected ranged data. Ultimately, I want to give the user the option of choosing that range as a plotted value. 

For example: 
You have a data frame of N repeated values from 1- 100  .
The DT is plotted with only unique values 1-100. 
Currently you can choose all 100 of the unique values and each unique value results in a grouping for plotting. 
I want to choose 1-50 and then 51-100 and have them plotted as just 2 plotted lines and groupings. 

So this is what I currently have plotted. 


And this is what I need 


Any ideas, thoughts, etc would be very helpful. 


Thank you for your time!


Amber James

Amber, you mentioned selecting columns, but you say that selected DT, I guess you mean data.tables, for row selection features. I don't know about selecting columns, but if you want to select rows, you can use two selectInput() statements, one for the start of your range and the other for the end of your range and then reference the respective index values. That works for rows, I don't see why it won't work for columns. I'm not exactly an ace programmer though.

If you use the development version of DT
(https://github.com/rstudio/DT), you will have access to the search
strings via input$tableId_search_columns:
http://rstudio.github.io/DT/shiny.html Note you have to process the
search string to get the range, e.g. the search string may be "2.87
... 3.90", and you will have to use functions like strsplit() and
as.numeric() to get a numeric vector of length 2.

Regards,
Yihui
